thread:
infra-bot: PAGER: [sev=high] multigpu-serving-runtime — anomalous collective failures detected in tp/pipeline groups (us-west-2)

sara: on it, grabbing logs and assigning

aj: i'm oncall, joining — seeing NCCL 'unreachable' + frequent CUDA Xid 79 from 3 different nodes

mike: quick snippet from node-gpu-14:
```
[2026-03-17T10:22:14Z] cudaDriver: Xid 79 GPU watchdog reset
[2026-03-17T10:22:14Z] nccl: NCCL ERROR Unreachable: communicator 0x7f8a...
[2026-03-17T10:22:16Z] containerd: container exit code 137 (oom/killed)
```

sara: thanks. container OOMs correlate w/ high KV-cache mem growth during long sequences. batch config was 16 -> spike.

cheng: @aj @sara pushed a quick patch to runtime to throttle batch until we stabilize — switching to single-GPU fallback for affected shards. deploying now.

aj: rolling update started. routing policy set to fallback-models for groups with >2 failures. duration ~1m per pod.

leo: recommending cordon of node-gpu-14 and drain in case of driver-level instability (avoid noisy restarts).
sara: agreed. cordon + drain in progress. migrating active serving traffic away.

mike: observed one noisy NIC flap on host during the window, might explain intermittent communicator disconnects. adding network team FYI.

oncall-bot: Handoff: aj -> sara at 10:28Z (sara has the lead).

aj: @sara status? do we need escalations / customer comms?

sara: mitigation applied: 1) batch size halved, 2) KV-cache TTL lowered, 3) fallback routing enabled, 4) cordoned node drain. Error rate for model endpoints dropped from 12% -> 1.5% over 6m.

cheng: rolling restart of affected containers completed. no new Xid 79s in last 3m on those hosts.

leo: customer impact: a subset of long-context jobs saw increased latency (tail +200–400ms) during fallback. no data exfiltration, requests served but prefetched/queued.

mike: capture for postmortem: reproduce path - long prefixes + batch=16 + mem fragmentation + NIC blip -> driver watchdog -> Xid79 -> NCCL unreachable -> container exit 137.

aj: temporary mitigation checklist posted to #eng-runtime: reduce batch, kvcache TTL, force fallback. will convert to runbook after postmortem.

infra-bot: Incident: status -> mitigated (service degraded -> restored) — monitoring will keep elevated thresholds for 1h.

sara: leaving notes and linking logs+trace in the incident ticket. assigning follow-up: driver upgrade validation (cheng), network flakiness triage (mike), runtime memory leak check (aj).

aj: signing off but will be reachable. thanks all :thumbsup:

sara: good work. closing pager but keeping handoff open for postmortem coordination.
